pr_comments: I'm not sure why this is needed? The system category was for internal use, documented as such and never used. How would this have caused issues?

Any entity registry stored that happened to have system as it's category. Could have been a custom component or anything that leaves it behind. Any time we end up removing any enums, we need to handle loading a store with enums not in the class.

> Any entity registry stored that happened to have system as it's category.

Nothing should have been using that?

It was available for 2 (?) releases. Since we removed it, we should just guard for `system` and replace it with `None` while loading and print a warning whenever an entity is added that has `system` category.
Here is a PR that just filters out system https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/71361
Fine by me.  I'd rather see a robust solution that avoids crashing if at all possible, but that fixes the immediate issue.
Since we guard the data that enters into storage, we shouldn't have to guard for any other bad data

issue_context.title: Removal of 'system' entity category causes crash due to existing entities in registry storage having that category.
issue_context.body:
### The problem

As per #68550, the 'system' entity category has been removed.

However, if there were any existing entities that were previously defined as the system entity_category now causes a crash on startup when home assistant tries to load the entity registry from storage.

Workaround was to manually edit core.entity_registry to remove the system entity_category.
Which is, I believe, not something that is generally intended for end users to perform?

Not sure if #71317 is related though.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.5.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

comments: Also, the removal of the entity_category doesn't appear to be listed as a breaking change in the release notes?
I can confirm that removing "system" (replacing it with `null`) solved the problem for me. 👍

> Which platform generated this entity?

For your reference, it was a custom mqtt sensor.
I don't believe the documentation for it at the time mentioned it was supposed to be internal only. So I used it to tag some of my own entities that were "internal" only.

review_comments: We should also test the logger message
I don't think we should just ignore every unknown value.
Breaking startup of home assistant due to a single errounous value here is not a good ide.
An alternative would be to  ignore the complete entity with bad data.

> Breaking startup of home assistant due to a single errounous value here is not a good ide.

There are thousands of ways custom integrations could break the registries 🤷

Have we pinpointed the root cause/code/integration?
Nope, we have two reported issues that i know of so far.
We should not define that as inline function, let's place that as standalone function into that file
